newsitem.title: USA: Calif Treasurer asks SEC to investigate muni deals.
newsitem.headline: Calif Treasurer asks SEC to investigate muni deals.

text.p: California state Treasurer Matt Fong sent letters to the Securities and Exchange Commission and California's Attorney General requesting an investigation of several municipal bond deals.
Fong alleged these bond offerings violated the "letter and spirit" of state law.
Fong released a list of nine projects, all of them underwritten by Pacific Genesis Group Inc.
An official with Pacific Genesis declined to comment early Thursday, saying he had yet to see Fong's letters.
Fong asked the SEC to investigate the following deals:

- $1.4 million taxable notes, Series C, issued in December 1995 by Sierra Central Valley agency. Agency members included Isleton, Waterford and the Chukchansi Indian Tribe of the Picayune Reservation.
- $6.975 million taxable notes, Series B, issued in December 1995 by Sierra Central Valley agency. Members included Isleton, Waterford and the Chukchansi Indian Tribe.
- $8.2 million revenue notes, Series A, issued in December 1995 by Sierra Central Valley agency. Members included Isleton, Waterford and the Chukchansi Indian Tribe.
- $7.075 million revenue bonds, issued in January 1996, by the California Commerce agency. Members included Mendota, Waterford and Georgetown Enterprises.
- $6.15 million bond anticipation notes, issued in February 1996, by the Malibu Canyon agency. Members included Mendota, Waterford and Georgetown Enterprises.

- $10 million bond anticipation notes, issued in March 1996, by the CA Desert agency. Members included Waterford, Merced Board of Education, Georgetown Enterprises and Pacific Rim Economic Development Corp.

- $3.05 million taxable revenue notes, issued in April 1996, by the California Commerce agency. Members included Waterford, Merced Board of Education, Georgetown Enterprises and Pacific Rim Economic Development Corp.
- $4.43 million revenue bonds, proposed to be issued on September 15, 1996, by the Lucerne Valley agency. Members include Waterford and Lucerne Valley Unified School District.

- $17.5 million revenue bonds, proposed to be issued on September 16, 1996, by the Pacific Ocean Estates agency. Members include Waterford, Merced Board of Education, Pacific Rim Economic Development Corp and Georgetown Enterprises.
